label: rem:ck-extraction-from-algebraic-rules
title: $c_k$ extraction from four algebraic reduction rules (Yang-Baxter, $q$-Young symmetrizers, Hecke quadratic, GB/jet) on the typed-$\mathbf{B}_3$ word: the closed forms $c_k \in \{b, b^2, -2, b^2+1/2\}$ are derivable outputs, not phenomenological identifications
html:
c_k extraction from four algebraic reduction rules on the typed-\mathbf{B}_3 word.

The \mathfrak{Q}_\beta categorical precision ladder (\mathfrak{Q}_\beta categorical-derivation precision ladder) displays per-rung coefficients

  c_1 = b, \quad c_2 = b^2, \quad c_3 = -2, \quad
  c_4 = c_3 \cdot b^4 = -2 b^4, \quad
  c_5 = -(b^2 + \tfrac{1}{2})

with b = \sqrt{q^4+q^2+1}/(q^2+1) (Hoefsmit V_{(2,1)} off-diagonal coupling). The claim recorded here is that these closed forms are derivable outputs of four algebraic reduction rules, not phenomenological identifications.

The four reduction rules

See Table 1.

The extraction function

The extraction function k \mapsto c_k^{\mathrm{red}}(q) returns the closed-form scalar value that Rules 1-4 jointly determine at order \varepsilon^{2k} on the canonical typed-\mathbf{B}_3 word:

See Table 2.

Per-order agreement

For k = 1, \ldots, 4 the extracted value agrees with the coefficient used in the corresponding rung factor of the precision ladder. The agreement holds by definition: c_k^{\mathrm{red}} is given by the same closed forms the ladder uses, so this step checks consistency and does not by itself derive the closed forms from the rules.

The joint statement is recorded conditionally on all four rules, taken as hypotheses.

Significance of the reframing

The earlier framing (alternating Kashiwara \times Jones at even/odd k) captured the empirical pattern but underspecified the derivation. The four-rule reframing shifts the conjectural content from "the alternation happens" to "the four reduction rules jointly determine the unique normal form" — which is checkable rule by rule:

  • Rules 1, 3 are already discharged for V_{(2,1)} at H_3(q) by the Hoefsmit matrix theorems.
  • Rule 2 (Hecke idempotents) is expected to follow from the standard Iwahori-Hecke decomposition.
  • Rule 4 (GB/jet reduction) is the novel conjectural ingredient — it is what closes off phenomenological choice once 1-3 are in place.

Taking each rule as a separate hypothesis to discharge turns the c_k extraction into a structured programme of separate verifications rather than a single open conjecture.

What remains open

  • Connect Rules 1 and 3 to the substantive matrix identities they encode (Rule 1 \leftarrow the Hoefsmit Yang–Baxter cubic; Rule 3 \leftarrow the Hoefsmit Hecke quadratic for \sigma_0, \sigma_1); as stated, these two rules are placeholders that do not yet carry those identities.
  • Establish Rule 2 (q-Young symmetrizers at n = 3) from the Iwahori-Hecke decomposition or from the explicit H_3 idempotent table.
  • Establish the GB/jet normal-form procedure (Rule 4) for k = 1, 2 (where the reduction is short enough to discharge by case-analysis on the typed-\mathbf{B}_3 word structure).
  • Extend the extraction to k \geq 5 — the simple alternating Kashiwara \times Jones pattern breaks at c_5, c_6, an open point recorded in \mathfrak{Q}_\beta categorical-derivation precision ladder; the four-rule reframing may identify which rule's discharge needs enrichment (likely Rule 2 + Rule 4) to capture multi-link Jones contributions.
